name: structura-base-intents
description: Canonical intent registry for the Structura semantic layer validator. All parser output is validated against this file. Intents are language-agnostic — they represent semantic meaning, not syntax.

import.description: Bringing an external module, package, or symbol into scope.

export.description: Exposing a symbol, value, or type for external consumption.

definition.description: Declaring a named, reusable code unit. Use the most specific sub-intent when possible.

function.description: Function, method, procedure, or constructor declaration.

class.description: Class, struct, interface, trait, protocol, or record declaration.

type.description: Type alias, type definition, or named type constraint.

examples.java: // via typedef patterns or generic bounds

variable.description: Variable, constant, or module-level field declaration.

namespace.description: Namespace, module block, or package-level scope declaration.

lambda.description: Anonymous function, arrow function, or closure assigned to a binding or passed as a value.

examples.go: fn := func(x int) int { return x * 2 }

call.description: Invoking a function, method, or constructor.

inheritance.description: A type extending, subclassing, or inheriting from another type.
inheritance.note: Prefer this over 'definition.class' when the inheritance relationship is the primary semantic signal.

examples.go: // via embedding: type Dog struct { Animal }
examples.rust: // no direct inheritance; use 'implementation' for trait impl

implementation.description: A type implementing an interface, trait, or protocol.

examples.javascript: class MyComp extends React.Component implements IClickable
examples.go: // implicit — struct satisfies interface by method set

decoration.description: A decorator, annotation, or attribute applied to a definition. Modifies or marks its target without being a call in the business-logic sense.

reference.description: A read-only usage of a symbol — accessing a value or type without calling it.

concurrency.description: Spawning concurrent work: goroutines, threads, async tasks, or parallel fibers.
concurrency.note: Only emit this intent when the concurrency boundary itself is semantically significant (e.g. tokio::spawn, go func(), Thread.start). Awaiting an already-async function is just a 'call'.

defer.description: Scheduling cleanup or teardown logic to run at scope exit, regardless of control flow.
defer.note: Intentionally narrow. Maps to Go's 'defer', Rust's 'Drop', Python's context managers (__exit__), and Java's try-with-resources. Do not use for general finally blocks.

examples.python: with open(f) as fp:  # __exit__ is the defer

intentResolution.description: How the validator resolves an intent string from a SemanticNode.
intentResolution.rule: An intent value is valid if it matches a top-level intent key OR a 'parentIntent.subIntent' dotted path (e.g. 'definition.function'). Both forms are accepted.

targetRequirement.description: Intents where 'target' MUST be present and non-empty on the SemanticNode.

locationFields.constraints: All values must be non-negative integers. 'end' must be >= 'start'.

rules: Extended intents MUST be declared in a parser-local 'extended-intents.json' with an 'extends' pointer to this file.
Extended intent keys MUST NOT shadow any key defined in this file.
Extended intent keys MUST be lowercase with underscores only.
Extended intents SHOULD still pass the same requiredNodeFields validation.
When a parser uses an extended intent, it MUST include a 'metadata.intentSource' field set to 'extended'.
